key_insight: A distributed QAOA-plus-classical-repair pipeline can scale quantum-assisted Minimum Birkhoff Decomposition to a 1,354-node, 1,710-variable problem by partitioning the task and preserving useful quantum sampling within each block.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical path for running constrained optimization on current superconducting hardware by reducing qubit demand, improving execution efficiency, and keeping candidate quality high enough for large-scale infrastructure problems.
method: Use spectral graph partitioning to split the native matching optimization into hardware-manageable subproblems.
Generate candidates with single-layer QAOA sampling, then apply greedy feasibility repair and E-FCFW updates to refine the decomposition.
Pack circuits spatially to reduce hardware execution time and support distributed execution on IBM quantum processors.
evidence_signal: On the PEGASE-1354 benchmark, repaired QAOA samples outperform simulated annealing and uniform random baselines in residual decomposition error, with 50-qubit partitions performing better than 20-qubit partitions and spatial packing cutting hardware time by about 3×.
watch_item: Performance depends on partition size and correlation retention, so overly small blocks or aggressive MPS truncation can weaken convergence and candidate quality.
paper_title: Scaling Quantum Optimization to the Thousand-Qubit Scale with Distributed Quantum Sampling
